title: After an elementary etale extension, a finite type algebra splits into a finite factor and a factor with no quasi-finite point over the chosen prime
statement: Let $R \to S$ be a ring map of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and let $\mathfrak p \subset R$ be a prime ideal. Then there are an etale ring map $R \to R'$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], a prime ideal $\mathfrak p' \subset R'$ lying over $\mathfrak p$ such that the induced map $\kappa(\mathfrak p) \to \kappa(\mathfrak p')$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-residue-field], and $R'$-algebras $A'$ and $B'$ with an $R'$-algebra isomorphism $R' \otimes_R S \cong A' \times B'$, such that $A'$ is a finitely generated $R'$-module and $R' \to B'$ is not quasi-finite [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime] at any prime ideal of $B'$ lying over $\mathfrak p'$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00UK (lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite, lines 40362-40420), with the finitely many finite factors A_1,...,A_n combined as A' = product_i A_i

proof.text: Replace S by its actual ULift to Type(max u v), transporting finite type by ULift.algEquiv. Prove a private auxiliary assertion by strong induction on an upper bound for the ncard of the isolated-point set of the fibre.

When the ncard is zero, finiteness of isolated points implies the set is empty. Use the identity R-algebra, P=p, A=PUnit (the zero ring), B=S, and TensorProduct.lid followed by AlgEquiv.uniqueProd.symm. The canonical residue-field map is the identity. A quasi-finite prime over p would give an isolated fibre point by the definition, contradicting emptiness.

For positive ncard apply the proved one-point-removal theorem. It constructs R₁,P₁,A₁,D and a decomposition R₁⊗_R S≃A₁×D with A₁ finite and strictly smaller fibre count for D. Invoke the strong induction hypothesis on R₁→D at P₁.

Compose the étale algebras using Algebra.Etale.comp and the lying-over relations using Ideal.LiesOver.trans. Prove equality of the composite canonical residue-field map with the composition using Ideal.ResidueField.ringHom_ext and map_algebraMap; compose their bijectivity proofs.

Use TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange, TensorProduct.congr, prodRight, prodCongr and the explicit product reassociation to identify R₂⊗_R S with ((R₂⊗_{R₁}A₁)×A₂)×B₂. Module.Finite.base_change and Module.Finite.prod give finiteness of the new A. The B₂ clause is exactly the induction hypothesis. Finally transport back from ULift S along TensorProduct.congr.

split_report.summary: Split Algebra Lemma 00UK by induction on the finite set of isolated points in the finite-type fibre. The base case is the empty finite factor; the induction step applies the reviewed 00UJ one-point etale/idempotent decomposition, removes the selected isolated point from the complementary factor, applies the induction hypothesis, and combines finite factors after a further etale base change using the Mathlib tensor-product product equivalence. The fibre comparison and non-quasi-finite conclusion are explicit.
